source_text: Ἄρειος ἡμῖν ὁ τῆς μανίας ἐπώνυμος τοῦ λόγου καὶ τῆς συνελεύσεως αἴτιος· ὃς, ὡς οὐκ ἴσμεν ὅπως, τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ τῆς Ἀλεξανδρέων ἐγκαταλεγεὶς Ἐκκλησίας, ἐλάνθανεν ἡμᾶς, τῆς τῶν τρισμακαρίων προφητῶν καὶ ἀποστόλων διδασκαλίας ὑπάρχων ἀλλότριος. Τὸν γὰρ μονογενῆ Υἱὸν καὶ Λόγον τοῦ Πατρὸς ἀποστερεῖν τῆς ὁμοουσιότητος τοῦ Πατρὸς οὐκ ἐντρέπεται, καὶ τῇ κτίσει τὸν κτίστην ὁ κτιστολάτρης συναριθμεῖν ἐπείγεται.
orientation: Eustathius is addressing Emperor Constantine and has just urged him to keep the faith walled about and let no heretic dishonor any person of the Trinity; now he names Arius as the source of the present disturbance.
pass_a_gloss: Arius, the namesake of the madness, is for us the cause of the word and of the assembly; who, as we do not know how, having been enrolled in the presbytery of the Church of the Alexandrians, was escaping our notice, being a stranger to the teaching of the thrice-blessed prophets and apostles. For he is not ashamed to deprive the only-begotten Son and Word of the Father of being consubstantial with the Father, and the worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator with creation.

lemmas.gloss: to number together with, count among

choices.why: Keeps the wordplay on Arius's name and the ironic epithet, matching the brief's identification of Arius as 'the namesake of the madness.'

choices.english: the cause of the word and of the assembly
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the ambiguity of λόγος (word/reason/account) and συνελεύσεως (assembly/gathering), which the source leaves open.
rejected: the cause of the dispute and the gathering
responsible for the argument and the meeting

choices.term: τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ τῆς Ἀλεξανδρέων ἐγκαταλεγεὶς Ἐκκλησίας

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle and the genitive of the city name, preserving the formal sense of official enrollment.

choices.why: Preserves the imperfect tense and the sense of ongoing concealment from Eustathius and the orthodox faithful.

choices.english: of the consubstantiality of the Father
choices.why: Uses the glossary English 'consubstantial' as the noun form, avoiding the banned 'homoousios' and 'of one substance.'
rejected: of the same substance as the Father

choices.english: the worshiper of what is created
choices.why: Uses the glossary English for κτιστολάτρης, preserving the ironic accusation that Arius treats the Creator as created.

pass_b_english: Arius is the one responsible for this word and this gathering—the namesake of the madness. Somehow, without our knowing how, he was enrolled in the presbytery of the Church of the Alexandrians, and he escaped our notice, though he was a stranger to the teaching of the thrice-blessed prophets and apostles. He is not ashamed to rob the only-begotten Son and Word of the Father of his consubstantiality with the Father, and this worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator together with creation.

problems.quote: this worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator together with creation
problems.why: Paradoxical insult: Arius 'worships creation' yet 'numbers Creator with creation'—logic unclear.
problems.fix: Check Greek; may mean 'this worshipper-of-the-created [Son] numbers the Creator with creation'.

edits.old: this worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator together with creation
edits.new: this worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator with creation

fixed: The English already says the same thing as the source: the worshiper of what is created (Arius) is eager to number the Creator with creation. The suggested alternative reading is not supported by the Greek text, which clearly has κτιστολάτρης as a nominative singular masculine noun in apposition to Arius, not as an adjective modifying the Son.

problems.why: Arius is not the namesake of madness itself but of the Arian heresy; 'namesake' misleads.
problems.fix: 'The one from whom the madness takes its name'.

edits.new: the one from whom the madness takes its name

fixed: The English already says exactly what the source says for the other confirmed problem; no change needed.

problems.quote: this worshiper of what is created
problems.why: Paradoxical insult: Arius worships the created Son, yet Eustathius means he degrades the Son to creature.
problems.fix: Clarify as 'one who worships a created being' or 'who makes the Son a creature'.

problems.why: Same concept (homoousios) but different part of speech and construction; reader may miss the link.
problems.fix: Use 'consubstantiality' consistently or gloss both as 'same-substance teaching'.

problems.why: 'Church' and 'fold of Christ' refer to the same body; reader may think two groups are meant.
problems.fix: Use 'Church' in both places or add 'the Church, the fold of Christ'.

problems.why: 'Word' likely means 'doctrine' or 'teaching,' not a single term; 'gathering' is vague.

problems.why: Core concept rendered as adjective in one place, noun in another; reader may miss connection.
problems.fix: Use 'consubstantial' consistently or gloss once: 'consubstantiality (oneness of substance)'.

problems.why: Singular vs. plural for same concept; minor but could suggest different categories of error.
problems.fix: Standardize to singular or plural throughout.

problems.quote: Somehow, without our knowing how, he was enrolled
problems.why: Unclear who 'our' refers to—Eustathius alone, a council, or Church leaders generally.
problems.fix: Clarify referent: 'without the Church's leaders knowing how' or 'without our knowing.'

problems.quote: this worshiper of a created being
problems.why: Arius worshiped Christ; calling him 'worshiper of a created being' is the charge, but phrasing is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Render as 'this man who worships what is created' to match the charge clearly.

The speaker problem about 'our' is not a mistranslation; the source uses first-person plural, and the English preserves it. No change is needed.

problems.quote: this man who worships what is created is eager to number the Creator with creation
problems.why: The logic seems inverted: Arius worships the Creator, not creation; Eustathius means Arius degrades the Creator-Son to creature status.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'this man who would worship what is created' or 'by making the Creator a creature'.

problems.quote: the only-begotten Son and Word of the Father
problems.why: Same divine person rendered three ways; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Use 'the Son' consistently or cross-reference on first use.
